parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: architecture
parameters.description: The target architecture of the image to register. Default: "x86_64"

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: billing_products
parameters.description: A list of valid billing codes. To be used with valid accounts by AWS Marketplace vendors.

parameters.name: boot_mode
parameters.description: The boot mode of the AMI. See the AWS documentation for more detail https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ami-boot.html. Support for uefi-preferred was added in release 8.2.0. Choices: "legacy-bios" "uefi" "uefi-preferred"

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: delete_snapshot
parameters.description: Delete snapshots when deregistering the AMI. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Human-readable string describing the contents and purpose of the AMI. Default: ""

parameters.name: device_mapping
parameters.description: List of device hashes/dictionaries with custom configurations (same block-device-mapping parameters).

parameters.name: delete_on_termination
parameters.description: Whether the device should be automatically deleted when the Instance is terminated. Choices: false true

parameters.name: device_name
parameters.description: The device name. For example /dev/sda.

parameters.name: encrypted
parameters.description: Whether the volume should be encrypted. Choices: false true

parameters.name: iops
parameters.description: When using device_mapping.volume_type=io1, this sets the number of IOPS provisioned for the volume.

parameters.name: no_device
parameters.description: Suppresses the specified device included in the block device mapping of the AMI. Choices: false true

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: The ID of the Snapshot.

parameters.name: virtual_name
parameters.description: The virtual name for the device. See the AWS documentation for more detail https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_BlockDeviceMapping.html.

parameters.name: volume_size
parameters.description: The size of the volume (in GiB).

parameters.name: volume_type
parameters.description: The volume type. Defaults to gp2 when not set.

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: enhanced_networking
parameters.description: A boolean representing whether enhanced networking with ENA is enabled or not. Choices: false true

parameters.name: image_id
parameters.description: Image ID to be deregistered.

parameters.name: image_location
parameters.description: The S3 location of an image to use for the AMI.

parameters.name: instance_id
parameters.description: Instance ID to create the AMI from.

parameters.name: kernel_id
parameters.description: The target kernel id of the image to register.

parameters.name: launch_permissions
parameters.description: Launch permissions for the AMI. You must pass all desired launch permissions if you wish to modify existing launch permissions (passing just groups will remove all users).

parameters.name: group_names
parameters.description: List of group names.

parameters.name: org_arns
parameters.description: List of The Amazon Resource Name(s) (ARN) of organization(s).

parameters.name: org_unit_arns
parameters.description: List of The Amazon Resource Name(s) (ARN) of an organizational unit(s) (OU).

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: List of account IDs.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the new AMI.

parameters.name: no_reboot
parameters.description: Flag indicating that the bundling process should not attempt to shutdown the instance before bundling. If this flag is true, the responsibility of maintaining file system integrity is left to the owner of the instance. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: purge_tags
parameters.description: If purge_tags=true and tags is set, existing tags will be purged from the resource to match exactly what is defined by tags parameter. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified, even if purge_tags=True. Tag keys beginning with aws: are reserved by Amazon and can not be modified. As such they will be ignored for the purposes of the purge_tags parameter. See the Amazon documentation for more information https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html#tag-conventions. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: ramdisk_id
parameters.description: The ID of the RAM disk.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: root_device_name
parameters.description: The root device name of the image to register.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: sriov_net_support
parameters.description: Set to simple to enable enhanced networking with the Intel 82599 Virtual Function interface for the AMI and any instances that you launch from the AMI.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Register or deregister an AMI. Choices: "absent" "present" ← (default)

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dictionary representing the tags to be applied to the resource. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified.

parameters.name: tpm_support
parameters.description: Set to v2.0 to enable Trusted Platform Module (TPM) support. If the image is configured for NitroTPM support, the value is v2.0. Requires boot_mode to be set to uefi. Requires an instance type that is compatible with Nitro. See the AWS documentation for more detail https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/nitrotpm.html.

parameters.name: uefi_data
parameters.description: Base64 representation of the non-volatile UEFI variable store. See the AWS documentation for more detail https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/uefi-secure-boot.html.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: virtualization_type
parameters.description: The virtualization type of the image to register. Default: "hvm"

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Wait for the AMI to be in state ‘available’ before returning. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: wait_timeout
parameters.description: How long before wait gives up, in seconds. Default: 1200

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.

- name: Basic AMI Creation
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    instance_id: i-xxxxxx
    wait: true
    name: newtest
    tags:
      Name: newtest
      Service: TestService

- name: Basic AMI Creation, without waiting
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    instance_id: i-xxxxxx
    wait: false
    name: newtest

- name: AMI Registration from EBS Snapshot
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    name: newtest
    state: present
    architecture: x86_64
    virtualization_type: hvm
    root_device_name: /dev/xvda
    device_mapping:
      - device_name: /dev/xvda
        volume_size: 8
        snapshot_id: snap-xxxxxxxx
        delete_on_termination: true
        volume_type: gp2

- name: AMI Creation, with a custom root-device size and another EBS attached
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    instance_id: i-xxxxxx
    name: newtest
    device_mapping:
      - device_name: /dev/sda1
        size: XXX
        delete_on_termination: true
        volume_type: gp2
      - device_name: /dev/sdb
        size: YYY
        delete_on_termination: false
        volume_type: gp2

- name: AMI Creation, excluding a volume attached at /dev/sdb
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    instance_id: i-xxxxxx
    name: newtest
    device_mapping:
      - device_name: /dev/sda1
        size: XXX
        delete_on_termination: true
        volume_type: gp2
      - device_name: /dev/sdb
        no_device: true

- name: AMI Creation with boot_mode and tpm_support
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    name: newtest
    state: present
    architecture: x86_64
    virtualization_type: hvm
    root_device_name: /dev/sda1
    device_mapping:
      - device_name: /dev/sda1
        snapshot_id: "{{ snapshot_id }}"
    wait: true
    region: us-east-1
    boot_mode: uefi
    uefi_data: data_file.bin
    tpm_support: v2.0

- name: Deregister/Delete AMI (keep associated snapshots)
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    image_id: "{{ instance.image_id }}"
    delete_snapshot: false
    state: absent

- name: Deregister AMI (delete associated snapshots too)
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    image_id: "{{ instance.image_id }}"
    delete_snapshot: true
    state: absent

- name: Update AMI Launch Permissions, making it public
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    image_id: "{{ instance.image_id }}"
    state: present
    launch_permissions:
      group_names: ['all']

- name: Allow AMI to be launched by another account
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    image_id: "{{ instance.image_id }}"
    state: present
    launch_permissions:
      user_ids: ['123456789012']

- name: Update AMI Launch Permissions, share AMI across an Organization and Organizational Units
  amazon.aws.ec2_ami:
    image_id: "{{ instance.image_id }}"
    state: present
    launch_permissions:
      org_arns: ['arn:aws:organizations::123456789012:organization/o-123ab4cdef']
      org_unit_arns: ['arn:aws:organizations::123456789012:ou/o-123example/ou-1234-5example']

return_values.name: architecture
return_values.description: Architecture of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "x86_64"

return_values.name: block_device_mapping
return_values.description: Block device mapping associated with image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: {"/dev/sda1": {"delete_on_termination": true, "encrypted": false, "size": 10, "snapshot_id": "snap-1a03b80e7", "volume_type": "standard"}}

return_values.name: creationDate
return_values.description: Creation date of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "2015-10-15T22:43:44.000Z"

return_values.name: description
return_values.description: Description of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "nat-server"

return_values.name: enhanced_networking
return_values.description: Specifies whether enhanced networking with ENA is enabled. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: true

return_values.name: hypervisor
return_values.description: Type of hypervisor. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "xen"

return_values.name: image_id
return_values.description: ID of the image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "ami-1234abcd"

return_values.name: image_owner_alias
return_values.description: The owner alias ( amazon | aws-marketplace). Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "amazon"

return_values.name: image_type
return_values.description: Type of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "machine"

return_values.name: is_public
return_values.description: Whether image is public. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: false

return_values.name: kernel_id
return_values.description: The kernel associated with the image, if any. Only applicable for machine images. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "aki-88aa75e1"

return_values.name: launch_permission
return_values.description: Permissions allowing other accounts to access the AMI. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: [{"group": "all"}]

return_values.name: location
return_values.description: Location of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "123456789012/nat-server"

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: AMI name of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "nat-server"

return_values.name: ownerId
return_values.description: Owner of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "123456789012"

return_values.name: platform
return_values.description: Platform of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "Windows"

return_values.name: product_codes
return_values.description: Any product codes associated with the AMI. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: []

return_values.name: ramdisk_id
return_values.description: The RAM disk associated with the image, if any. Only applicable for machine images. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists

return_values.name: root_device_name
return_values.description: Root device name of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "/dev/sda1"

return_values.name: root_device_type
return_values.description: Root device type of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "ebs"

return_values.name: snapshots_deleted
return_values.description: A list of snapshot ids deleted after deregistering image. Returned: after AMI is deregistered, if delete_snapshot=true Sample: ["snap-fbcccb8f", "snap-cfe7cdb4"]

return_values.name: sriov_net_support
return_values.description: Specifies whether enhanced networking with the Intel 82599 Virtual Function interface is enabled. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "simple"

return_values.name: state
return_values.description: State of image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "available"

return_values.name: state_reason
return_values.description: The reason for the state change. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: {"Code": "string", "Message": "string"}

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: A dictionary of tags assigned to image. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: {"Env": "devel", "Name": "nat-server"}

return_values.name: virtualization_type
return_values.description: Image virtualization type. Returned: when AMI is created or already exists Sample: "hvm"
